regulatory_note: Med SOx-ECA + FuelEU Maritime apply. Barcelona's port + city governments are actively capping cruise calls and shifting cruise traffic away from the central port — favouring clean high-frequency water shuttles. The Medes Islands MPA and Cap de Creus Natural Park add citable quiet-mode/zero-wake regulatory anchors on the Costa Brava leg.
seasonality: Mediterranean — summer peak June–September on Costa Brava, year-round commuter base on the Barcelona waterfront, shoulder months that work cleanly under the cruise-cap regime. The corridor sits behind Cap de Creus / Costa Brava lee for the prevailing NW; only true open-Med Balearic spokes see real winter weather.

summary: Barcelona is an urban-volume plus premium-charter coastal corridor. The Port of Barcelona is Europe's #1 / world's #4 cruise base (~3.9M cruise passengers) and is now actively scaling back amid overtourism backlash — a textbook signal to shift volume to clean, high-frequency water shuttles (Barcelona waterfront commuter, Barcelona → Costa Brava → Cadaqués). The Costa Brava — Palamós, the Medes MPA, Cadaqués — adds the charter top-end. Med SOx-ECA, Barcelona's own port air-quality and cruise-cap politics, and the Medes marine reserve are the regulatory levers. Water geography is linear coast (no island lattice) which caps the score; Barcelona↔Balearics (~120 nm) is the Quanta spoke.
tagline: Europe's #1 cruise base is actively capping cruise growth — a textbook signal to shift volume to clean high-frequency water shuttles.
